equities.name: TSX Composite
equities.context: Banks advanced on rate expectations; energy slumped on WTI collapse from $128 peak
equities.commentary: The S&P/TSX Composite closed near 34,270 on April 18, approaching February record highs.1 Financials led the advance — BMO gained +1.65% and Scotiabank added +2.03% — as bond market repricing of BoC tightening supported bank earnings expectations. Energy weighed: CNRL fell -7.28% and Suncor declined -4% as WTI collapsed 34% from its early-April peak before stabilizing.2 The broad S&P/TSX 60 gained +6.29% over the past month and +43.06% year-over-year.1

equities.name: S&P 500
equities.context: Defensive positioning amid geopolitical uncertainty; tech underperformed
equities.commentary: The S&P 500 traded near 5,282, underperforming the TSX over the period as U.S. consumer sentiment fell to 50.8 — the second-lowest reading since 1952.3 The Fed held rates at 3.50%-3.75% with March minutes indicating willingness to consider increases.4 U.S. nonfarm payrolls added +178,000 jobs with unemployment at 4.3%.4

equities.name: Dow Jones
equities.context: Industrials mixed on tariff uncertainty; defensive sectors outperformed
equities.commentary: The Dow Jones Industrial Average traded near 39,140, weighed by U.S. Section 232 tariff restructuring — 50% duties on aluminum, steel, and copper.5 Canada's 6-month pause on retaliatory tariffs (announced April 15) provided partial relief for cross-border manufacturing exposure.5 The CUSMA joint review scheduled for July 2026 remains an overhang for 45 tracked Canadian manufacturing projects valued at $67.3B.6

equities.name: NASDAQ
equities.context: Growth stocks pressured by rate-hike repricing globally
equities.commentary: The NASDAQ Composite traded near 16,320, underperforming broader indices as global central banks shifted toward tightening.4 The BoC, Fed, and ECB all face decisions within the April 29-30 window, with markets pricing potential increases from each institution.4 Higher discount rates compress growth valuations across the technology and clean-energy sectors that overlap with Canada's 550 tracked power and energy projects.6
